material.text: @leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar: Renders open session tabs as a Sessions block at the bottom of the OpenCode sidebar

type=plugin source=npm:@leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar created=2026-10-14T07:20:07.872Z firstSeen=2026-11-03T14:29:15.298Z published=2026-11-20T17:49:24.715Z maintainers=leo.gimp repoId=1377255509 stars=3 npm30d=?

# @leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 TUI plugin that renders open sessions as a **Sessions** block at the bottom of the sidebar - click a row to switch sessions, `×` to close one, or switch with the keyboard (`ctrl+tab` / `ctrl+shift+tab` / `ctrl+1..0`) - and takes over the built-in top tab strip. While the plugin is installed, `tabs.mode` is forced to `"off"` in `cli.json`; uninstalling unmounts the block and releases the setting.


## Install This is a TUI (CLI-only) plugin, so it belongs in **`cli.json`** under the **`plugins`** key - not in `opencode.json(c)`, and not in a `tui.json`. `tui.json` was the OpenCode v1 layout and is not read by v2. ### From npm (recommended) ```bash opencode plugin add "@leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar" ``` Or add it by hand to `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": ["@leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar"] } ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > The npm package is **scoped to `@leo.gimp`**. The unscoped `opencode-sessions-sidebar` name on npm belongs to a different, unrelated plugin by another author - installing that name gets you their plugin, not this one. ### From source Point `plugins` at the checkout: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": ["C:\\path\\to\\sessions-sidebar"] } ``` Relative paths (`./plugins/sessions-sidebar`), `file://` URLs, and dropping the folder into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` all work too. The published tarball ships the TypeScript sources as-is - there is no build step to run. ### Uninstall ```bash opencode plugin remove "@leo.gimp/opencode-sessions-sidebar" ``` Or delete the entry from `cli.json`. Either way the plugin stops enforcing its settings and the Sessions block is unmounted. Because the plugin forces `tabs.mode: "off"` for as long as it is installed - deliberately not restoring anything while it runs - set **Mode** back (Settings → Tabs → Mode) after uninstalling if you want the built-in strip again. To turn the plugin off temporarily without uninstalling it, prefix its id with `-` (`opencode plugin list` shows the ids in use): ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": ["-sessions-sidebar"] } ``` `cli.json` is watched, so config changes are picked up without restarting OpenCode. Edits to the plugin's own source files are not watched - restart the TUI after changing them. ## Features
### Sessions block A live list of open sessions appended to the bottom of the sidebar content area, above the built-in footer directory indicator: - One row per session: **status icon + title**, the active session highlighted in bold - **Click a row to switch** to that session, click **`×`** to remove it from the list - A **`+ New session`** row creates a new session and switches to it - Closing the active session switches to the next remaining session (or home when the list is empty) - the session itself stays in the history, exactly like the old tab strip's close - Deleting a session (from the session manager, another window, or the CLI) **removes its row immediately**; if it was the session being viewed, the view switches to the neighbouring session - Tracks up to **10 sessions**, newest at the bottom; the order is append-only, so rows never shuffle while you work, and the active session is never evicted by the cap - The list is **live-synced across every open window** - appends and removals are computed against the persisted state under a file lock, so two windows can never duplicate or drop each other's rows - Session titles persist in the plugin's store (kept fresh via rename events), so they survive data eviction; untitled sessions render as `New session · 3m`-style labels ### Keyboard The built-in strip's keymap dies with the strip, so the plugin re-binds the same keys to its own list (all commands also appear in the palette under **Sessions**): | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | `ctrl+tab` / `ctrl+shift+tab` | Next / previous session | | `ctrl+1` … `ctrl+0` | Open session 1 … 10 | | `w` | Close the current session | | `ctrl+shift+t` | Reopen the last closed session | ### Status indicators Each row's icon mirrors the built-in tab strip logic, across the session and its whole subagent family - distinct shapes, not just colors, so they stay readable on any terminal: - **`!`** - a permission prompt is waiting (warning colour) - **`?`** - a question form is waiting (warning colour) - **`●`** - busy: breathing (smooth cosine pulse) while the agent is responding or has pending work; static when `animations` is set to `false` in `cli.json` (read once at startup) - **`•`** - unread: the session finished working after you last looked at it - **`○`** - idle ### Tab strip ownership While the plugin is **installed**, the built-in top tab strip stays forced off: it sets `tabs.mode: "off"` in `cli.json` (session tracking moves into the plugin, because the built-in tab store stops tracking once the strip is disabled), and it keeps that setting locked for as long as the plugin stays installed: - **Forced off all the time** - the value is not temporarily flipped and restored on exit; it stays `"off"` across restarts, so Settings always shows Tabs → Mode: **off** - If the setting is changed while the plugin runs - e.g. toggled in the settings dialog - the plugin re-asserts `"off"` by watching the config file; the TUI re-reads `cli.json` on every file change, so the change snaps back within ~150 ms - Only **uninstalling** the plugin releases the lock - re-enable the strip in Settings (Tabs → Mode) at that point - The plugin writes `mode` and deletes the legacy `enabled` boolean, so the two keys can never disagree - `cli.json` is resolved like OpenCode does (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `~/.config/opencode`) and is created when missing; writes are atomic (temp + rename). If the file cannot be parsed (e.g. JSONC comments), a toast asks you to hide the strip manually ## Notes - The sidebar row width is fixed by OpenCode's sidebar layout; long titles are clipped with a trailing ellipsis, counting terminal display columns so CJK/emoji titles cannot overflow the row. - `index.ts` is a deliberate no-op so the server-side plugin loader resolves the package cleanly without pulling TUI-only dependencies into the server module map - all rendering lives in `tui.tsx`, which is what the `./tui` export loads. - `@opencode/plugin`, `@opentui/core`, `@opentui/solid` and `solid-js` are declared as real dependencies so the bare specifiers resolve inside OpenCode's plugin install cache. The header comment in `tui.tsx` mentions `@opentui/solid` only as a `@jsxImportSource` pragma, but the JSX runtime must still be importable by name in the installed cache. - `solid-js` tracks `^1.9.15` - what the OpenCode TUI is built against - rather than the exact `1.9.12` that `@opentui/solid` still peers on, which would pull a `seroval` with four unfixed critical advisories. npm is strict about that stale peer, so the repo ships a `.npmrc` that relaxes it; OpenCode installs plugins with Bun, which does not care. ## Requirements - OpenCode **2.0.0+** (uses the V2 TUI plugin slot API and `cli.json`) ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
